name: ANSI/IEEE ampere-hour meter symbol
summary: IEEE-library ampere-hour meter form for integrating charge in DC circuits such as battery and plating supplies.
description: An ampere-hour meter integrates current over time and is most often drawn in DC battery, charger and electrochemical supply circuits. It is normally fed from a shunt, so the schematic should show the shunt, its millivolt rating and the polarity of the sensing leads alongside the meter.

The symbol does not say whether the register counts charge in one direction only or nets charge and discharge. Battery state-of-charge estimation depends on that setting and on efficiency correction, neither of which is visible from the instrument form.
readingNotes: Find the shunt or sensor that supplies the current signal.
Confirm whether the register is unidirectional or bidirectional.
distinction: An ampere-hour meter accumulates charge; an ammeter shows instantaneous current and a kWh meter accumulates energy.
